name: WE-031 building energy code (expand-loop blind run)

unclear.text: The size adjustment: the Act requires the Energy Office to adjust the index for dwelling size, no rule has been made.
readings: U1-a: no adjustment beyond the per-square-foot measure
U1-b: for homes above 2,500 square feet the maximum applies to the home's total modeled energy as if it were 2,500 square feet

a1.text: The schedule outpaces the counterfactual improvement, so that from about Year 4 a material share of the homes that would have been built would not meet the standard.

a2.text: Building departments do not issue permits without a DEI report, nor certificates of occupancy without a rater's certificate.

a10.text: Building departments' review staff is fixed in the short run, because fees are fixed by ordinance and are not raised within two years.

a20.text: Buyers of homes and land expect the schedule to be carried out, not paused.

a25.text: The Energy Office's audit unit is funded by a new general-fund appropriation, as K3 says, not by cuts elsewhere.

a28.text: Under a per-square-foot index, a larger home meets a given maximum at lower cost per square foot, because loads that do not grow with floor area (water heating, appliances) are spread over more of it.
